The "select and place" idea doesn't work either. The only interactive elements are the 5 Γ toggles.
Let me think about this very carefully. The 5 Γ toggles are the only interactive elements. The initial state was B,w,B,w,w. I need to figure out what pattern to set.
Wait — let me reconsider the shape of the Γ toggles. Each toggle is:
```
X X X   (row 42, cols c..c+2)
X . .   (row 44, col c)
X . .   (row 45, col c)
X . .   (row 46, col c)
```
Wait, let me re-verify. From the ASCII:
Row 42: bar at cols 20-22 (T1), 25-27 (T2), 30-32 (T3), 35-37 (T4), 40-42 (T5)
Row 44: stem at col 20 (T1), 25 (T2), 30 (T3), 35 (T4), 40 (T5)
Row 45: stem at col 20, 25, 30, 35, 40
Row 46: stem at col 20, 25, 30, 35, 40
So each toggle is a "Γ" (gamma) shape: a horizontal bar of 3 cells at the top, and a vertical stem of 3 cells extending downward from the left end of the bar.
So the shape is:
```
# # #
# . .
# . .
# . .
```
This is like a "flag" or "corner" shape.
Now, the 5 toggles are at cols 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, spaced 5 apart. The board is cols 14-49 (width 36). The piece is at cols 30-33.
Hmm, wait. What if these 5 Γ shapes are actually the "walls" of a "ball maze," and the ball bounces between them? The ball is at the bottom (cols 32-40). The toggles are at the bottom of the board (rows 42-46). If the ball is launched upward, it would enter the board and bounce off the checkerboard... no, that's not right.
Actually, let me reconsider. What if the 5 Γ toggles are "pegs" or "bumpers" inside a "Peggle"-style game, and the ball is launched from the bottom? The ball is at the bottom (rows 51-59). The toggles are at rows 42-46, just below the board (the board ends at row 41). So the toggles are between the board and the ball.
If the ball is launched upward, it would first hit the toggle region (rows 42-46), then enter the board (rows 9-41). The toggles (as bumpers) would deflect the ball. The goal might be to get the ball to hit the yellow piece, or to drop the piece into the cup.
But I still can't launch the ball. Let me try harder.
Actually — wait. Let me reconsider. What if the ball is launched by clicking the white tab, and the tab is a "slingshot"? I clicked (49,42), but nothing happened. Let me try clicking the tab at different positions, or try clicking the ball and then the tab.
Or — what if the game is "Peggle"-style, and the ball is launched by clicking anywhere on the board (the ball is fired from the bottom toward the click point)? Let me try clicking inside the board (e.g., row 20, col 31) and see if the ball launches.
Let me try that.
